goldens.comment: The EmbeddableHost model's before_validation callback calls self.host.sub! to strip http://, https://, and path segments, but if self.host is nil, this raises NoMethodError.

The update and destroy methods in Admin::EmbeddableHostsController do not validate the existence of the EmbeddableHost record retrieved by ID. If EmbeddableHost.where(id: params[:id]).first returns nil (i.e., the host does not exist), attempting to call methods on the nil object (e.g., save_host or destroy) will result in a NoMethodError.
record_for_host compares lower(host) = ? but does not normalize the parameter’s case, so mixed‑case referer hosts may fail to match even though comparison intends to be case‑insensitive.

Because this migration inserts embeddable_hosts rows with raw SQL, any existing embeddable_hosts values that include http:// or /https:// or path segments won’t go through the EmbeddableHost model’s normalization, so the new host lookup (which compares only the bare host) may fail for migrated data. Consider ensuring that migrated hosts are normalized to the same format as newly created EmbeddableHost records so existing embedding configurations keep working.

The contents of `category_fabricator.rb` and `embeddable_host_fabricator.rb` have been swapped, resulting in the loss of original category fabricators and potentially causing errors in fabricator usage.

The SQL query in the `app/controllers/admin/embeddable_hosts_controller.rb` file uses string interpolation (`'#{h}'`) to insert values, which is vulnerable to SQL injection. It should use parameter binding or proper quoting to prevent this security vulnerability.

The migration accesses execute(...)[0]['id'] without checking if the query returned any rows, which causes a crash when no embed_category setting exists. This can lead to a broken feature when attempting to edit category/host relationships.

adjudication_records.issue_text: db/migrate/20150818190757_create_embeddable_hosts.rb:11 — The migration dereferences the first category query row before checking it, so sites without an embed_category override abort the upgrade

db/migrate/20150818190757_create_embeddable_hosts.rb:25 — Legacy URL-form hosts are inserted without model normalization, so previously accepted values such as https://example.com/path stop matching after upgrade
db/migrate/20150818190757_create_embeddable_hosts.rb:31 — Irreversible execute statements inside change make database rollback fail and cannot restore the deleted legacy settings

adjudication.rationale: The migration uses `change` method but contains `execute` statements that delete data from site_settings table (line 31: `execute "DELETE FROM site_settings WHERE name IN ('embeddable_hosts', 'embed_category')"`). Rails cannot automatically reverse raw SQL execute statements, so if this migration needs to be rolled back, it will fail and the deleted settings data will be permanently lost. The migration should either use `up`/`down` methods with explicit rollback logic, or avoid destructive operations in a `change` block.

adjudication_records.issue_text: app/models/embeddable_host.rb:17 — Duplicate hosts are allowed and record_for_host uses an unordered first row, making the category assignment nondeterministic

adjudication.rationale: The finding identifies a real issue. Looking at the diff, EmbeddableHost model (app/models/embeddable_host.rb) has no unique constraint on the host field - the validation only checks format, not uniqueness. The record_for_host method uses `.first` without any ordering, and the controller's save_host method doesn't check for duplicates before saving. This means duplicate hosts can be created, and when record_for_host is called (used in topic_embed.rb to determine category_id for embedded posts), it will return an arbitrary record, making category assignment nondeterministic. The migration also doesn't add a unique index on the host column.

adjudication_records.issue_text: app/controllers/admin/embeddable_hosts_controller.rb:24 — Arbitrary or subsequently deleted category IDs remain valid host mappings and are later passed into topic creation as stale category references

adjudication.rationale: The finding claims that arbitrary or deleted category IDs remain valid and cause stale references. Looking at the diff, the code in embeddable_hosts_controller.rb line 24 sets category_id to uncategorized_category_id if blank, and the EmbeddableHost model has a belongs_to :category association. When a topic is created in topic_embed.rb, it uses eh.try(:category_id) which would return nil if the category was deleted (since the association would be nil). The finding misreads the code - there's no evidence of stale category references being passed through. The category_id is validated through the belongs_to association, and if a category is deleted, standard Rails behavior would handle this.

adjudication_records.issue_text: app/models/embeddable_host.rb:2 — The host validator rejects valid modern domains whose top-level label exceeds five characters, preventing common allowed hosts from being saved

adjudication.rationale: The diff shows the regex validator on line 2 of app/models/embeddable_host.rb: `/\A[a-z0-9]+([\-\.]{1}[a-z0-9]+)*\.[a-z]{2,5}(:[0-9]{1,5})?(\/.*)?\Z/i`. The `[a-z]{2,5}` part limits TLDs to 2-5 characters. Modern TLDs like .technology (10 chars), .photography (11 chars), .engineering (11 chars), etc. would be rejected. This is a real bug that prevents valid domains from being saved as embeddable hosts.

adjudication_records.issue_text: app/models/embeddable_host.rb:17 — Ports accepted and stored by validation can never match because URI.host discards the request port before lookup

adjudication.rationale: The finding identifies a real bug. Looking at the diff, the EmbeddableHost model validates hosts with a regex that allows ports (:[0-9]{1,5}), and the before_validation strips the protocol and path but preserves the port. However, in the record_for_host method (lines 10-17), it uses URI(host).host which returns only the hostname without the port. So if a user saves 'example.com:8080' as an embeddable host, the lookup using URI('http://example.com:8080').host would return 'example.com', which wouldn't match 'example.com:8080' stored in the database. This is a legitimate correctness bug where hosts with ports can be stored but will never match during lookup.

adjudication_records.issue_text: config/site_settings.yml:761 — Removing embeddable_hosts and embed_category drops the established SiteSetting/admin-settings API without a compatibility path, breaking plugins and automation on upgrade

adjudication.rationale: The diff shows removal of 'embeddable_hosts' and 'embed_category' from config/site_settings.yml (lines 762-763 removed). The migration in db/migrate/20150818190757_create_embeddable_hosts.rb migrates existing data to the new EmbeddableHost model and then deletes these settings. While this is a breaking change for any plugins or external automation that relied on these SiteSettings, it's not a bug per se - it's a deliberate architectural change. However, the finding raises a valid concern about backward compatibility for existing integrations. The migration does handle data migration, but any code directly accessing SiteSetting.embeddable_hosts or SiteSetting.embed_category would break.

adjudication_records.issue_text: db/migrate/20150818190757_create_embeddable_hosts.rb:25 — Migrating host strings verbatim breaks previously accepted URL-form values because the new lookup compares only URI.host against the stored value

adjudication.rationale: The migration at line 25 copies host values verbatim from the old site_settings table (which could contain URLs like 'http://example.com' or 'https://example.com') into the new embeddable_hosts table. However, the new EmbeddableHost model's before_validation callback strips 'http://' and 'https://' prefixes, and the host_allowed? method compares URI(host).host against the stored value. If the migration inserts 'http://example.com' directly without stripping the protocol, the comparison in host_allowed? will fail because URI('http://eviltrout.com').host returns 'eviltrout.com' but the stored value would be 'http://eviltrout.com'. The migration should strip the protocol prefix before inserting, or use the model's save method to trigger the before_validation callback.

adjudication_records.issue_text: app/assets/javascripts/discourse/models/store.js.es6:200 — Plural relationship hydration deletes every *_ids field even when lookup fails, silently changing existing model shapes to arrays containing undefined entries

adjudication.rationale: Looking at the diff in store.js.es6 lines 192-210, when handling plural relationships (m[2] is truthy for '_ids' suffix), the code maps over obj[k] to hydrate each id via _lookupSubType. However, _lookupSubType can return undefined/null if the lookup fails. The code then assigns this potentially undefined-containing array with `obj[self.pluralize(subType)] = hydrated || [];` and always deletes the original key with `delete obj[k]`. This means if any lookup fails, the array will contain undefined entries, and the original _ids field is always removed regardless of success. In contrast, the singular case (else branch) only deletes obj[k] when hydration succeeds (`if (hydrated)`). This asymmetry means plural relationships silently corrupt data when lookups fail.

adjudication_records.issue_text: config/routes.rb:153 — Declaring the full resources route exposes index and show endpoints that the controller does not implement

adjudication.rationale: Looking at the diff, line 153 in config/routes.rb shows `resources :embeddable_hosts, constraints: AdminConstraint.new`. The Admin::EmbeddableHostsController in the diff implements create, update, and destroy actions. While it's true that index and show are not implemented, Rails resources routes are commonly used even when not all actions are implemented - unimplemented actions will simply return 404 or routing errors. This is standard Rails practice and not a bug. The controller inherits from Admin::AdminController which provides authentication, so there's no security issue. This is at most a minor optimization suggestion to use `only:` to restrict routes, not a real defect.

adjudication_records.issue_text: db/migrate/20150818190757_create_embeddable_hosts.rb:11 — An unset or nonmatching embed_category makes the SELECT return no row, so indexing `[0]['id']` aborts the migration before its fallback can run.

adjudication_records.issue_text: app/models/embeddable_host.rb:17 — Duplicate host rows are allowed while lookup selects an unordered first row, making the category for a duplicated host nondeterministic.

adjudication.rationale: The finding is valid. Looking at the diff, `EmbeddableHost` model (app/models/embeddable_host.rb) has no unique constraint on the `host` column - the migration at db/migrate/20150818190757_create_embeddable_hosts.rb creates the table with just `t.string :host, null: false` without any uniqueness validation or index. The `record_for_host` method uses `.first` without any ordering, and the model has no `validates_uniqueness_of :host`. This means duplicate hosts can be inserted, and when looking up which category to use, the result is nondeterministic since `.first` without explicit ordering depends on database implementation.

adjudication_records.issue_text: app/models/embeddable_host.rb:17 — Hosts saved with an allowed port suffix can never match because URI parsing removes the request port before comparing it with the stored `host:port` value.

adjudication.rationale: Looking at the diff, in `app/models/embeddable_host.rb`, the `before_validation` callback strips the protocol and path from the host (`self.host.sub!(/^https?:\/\//, '')` and `self.host.sub!(/\/.*$/, '')`), but it does NOT strip the port. The validation regex allows ports: `/\A[a-z0-9]+([\-\.]{1}[a-z0-9]+)*\.[a-z]{2,5}(:[0-9]{1,5})?(\/.*)?\Z/i`. So a host like 'example.com:8080' can be saved. However, in `record_for_host`, it uses `uri = URI(host)` and then `host = uri.host`. The `URI.host` method returns just the hostname WITHOUT the port (the port is in `uri.port`). So if you save 'example.com:8080' and then check against a URL like 'http://example.com:8080/page', the comparison `where("lower(host) = ?", host)` will compare 'example.com' (from URI parsing) against 'example.com:8080' (stored), which will never match. This is a real bug.

adjudication_records.issue_text: app/models/embeddable_host.rb:2 — The five-character TLD limit rejects valid embeddable domains such as `example.museum`, preventing admins from adding or editing those hosts.

adjudication.rationale: The diff shows in app/models/embeddable_host.rb line 2 a regex validation: `/\A[a-z0-9]+([\-\.]{1}[a-z0-9]+)*\.[a-z]{2,5}(:[0-9]{1,5})?(\/.*)?\Z/i`. The `[a-z]{2,5}` part limits TLDs to 2-5 characters. Valid TLDs like `.museum` (6 chars), `.technology` (10 chars), and many new gTLDs exceed this limit and would be rejected by this validation, preventing admins from adding legitimate embeddable hosts.

adjudication_records.issue_text: app/controllers/admin/embeddable_hosts_controller.rb:24 — Arbitrary or concurrently deleted category IDs are persisted without existence validation and are later assigned to newly imported topics.

adjudication.rationale: The finding identifies a real issue in the diff. In app/controllers/admin/embeddable_hosts_controller.rb lines 21-24, the save_host method accepts category_id from params and assigns it directly to the host without validating that the category actually exists. If category_id is blank, it defaults to uncategorized_category_id, but if a non-existent category_id is provided, it will be persisted. Later in app/models/topic_embed.rb lines 36-44, when importing topics, the code uses eh.try(:category_id) which would pass this potentially invalid category_id to PostCreator. The EmbeddableHost model (app/models/embeddable_host.rb) has 'belongs_to :category' but no validation ensuring the category exists. This could lead to topics being created with invalid category references.

adjudication_records.issue_text: app/assets/javascripts/admin/components/embeddable-host.js.es6:46 — Delete request failures are left as unhandled promise rejections, so admins receive no error feedback when a host cannot be removed.

adjudication.rationale: Looking at the delete action in embeddable-host.js.es6 lines 42-49, the code calls `this.get('host').destroyRecord().then(...)` but there is no `.catch()` handler for the promise. If the destroyRecord() call fails (e.g., network error, server error), the promise rejection will be unhandled and the user will receive no feedback about the failure. This contrasts with the save() action which properly uses `.catch(popupAjaxError)` to handle errors. This is a real bug where error handling is missing.

adjudication_records.issue_text: db/migrate/20150818190757_create_embeddable_hosts.rb:11 — Dereferencing row zero before checking for a missing embed_category setting makes the migration crash on default or unset configurations instead of using the fallback category.
matched_golden_ids: The migration accesses execute(...)[0]['id'] without checking if the query returned any rows, which causes a crash when no embed_category setting exists. This can lead to a broken feature when attempting to edit category/host relationships.
adjudication_records.primary_judge_reasoning: The candidate issue identifies the exact same problem as the golden comment - accessing row zero (execute(...)[0]['id']) without first checking if the query returned any rows when no embed_category setting exists. Both describe the same bug: the migration crashes when there's no embed_category setting because it tries to dereference index 0 on an empty result set.

adjudication_records.issue_text: db/migrate/20150818190757_create_embeddable_hosts.rb:25 — Copying legacy URL-form host entries verbatim leaves values such as https://example.com/path unmatched by the new hostname-only lookup after upgrade.

adjudication.rationale: The migration at line 25 copies legacy host values verbatim with `execute "INSERT INTO embeddable_hosts (host, category_id, created_at, updated_at) VALUES ('#{h}', ...)"`. The old `embeddable_hosts` setting could contain URLs like 'https://example.com/path' (as shown in the test at line 73 of embed_controller_spec.rb: `'https://example.com/1234'`). The new EmbeddableHost model's `before_validation` strips protocols and paths, but this only runs on new records created through the model, not on raw SQL inserts in the migration. The `host_allowed?` method does `where("lower(host) = ?", host)` comparing against just the hostname extracted from the URL. So migrated entries like 'https://example.com/1234' won't match lookups for 'example.com', breaking embedding for upgraded sites.

adjudication_records.issue_text: db/migrate/20150818190757_create_embeddable_hosts.rb:31 — Deleting the only legacy host and category settings inside an irreversible change migration leaves a rolled-back application with embedding disabled and no way to restore the configuration.

adjudication.rationale: The migration at db/migrate/20150818190757_create_embeddable_hosts.rb uses `def change` which Rails treats as reversible, but the migration contains `execute "DELETE FROM site_settings WHERE name IN ('embeddable_hosts', 'embed_category')"` at line 31. This DELETE statement is not automatically reversible - if the migration is rolled back, the old site_settings data would be permanently lost with no way to restore it. This is a legitimate concern about data loss during rollback scenarios, though it's an architectural/design issue rather than a bug in normal forward operation.

adjudication_records.issue_text: spec/fabricators/category_fabricator.rb:1 — The embeddable-host fabricator replaced the category definitions while those definitions moved into the oppositely named file, breaking convention-based fixture loading and coupling unrelated fixtures.
matched_golden_ids: The contents of `category_fabricator.rb` and `embeddable_host_fabricator.rb` have been swapped, resulting in the loss of original category fabricators and potentially causing errors in fabricator usage.
adjudication_records.primary_judge_reasoning: The candidate issue identifies the same problem as the golden comment - that the contents of category_fabricator.rb and embeddable_host_fabricator.rb have been swapped. The candidate mentions 'embeddable-host fabricator replaced the category definitions while those definitions moved into the oppositely named file', which is exactly the file swap issue described in the golden comment. Both point to the same underlying bug of fabricator contents being in the wrong files.

adjudication_records.issue_text: app/assets/javascripts/admin/controllers/admin-embedding.js.es6:5 — The unreferenced saveChanges action drives a no-op backend update endpoint, leaving a dead write path that should be removed until embedding-level state is editable.

adjudication.rationale: The finding correctly identifies that saveChanges action in admin-embedding.js.es6 calls `this.get('embedding').update({})` with an empty object, and the backend update endpoint in embedding_controller.rb simply re-renders the same data without actually updating anything. This is indeed a no-op write path. However, this appears to be intentional scaffolding for future functionality (the embedding settings UI is being built incrementally). While it's a valid architectural concern about dead code, it's not a bug since it doesn't cause incorrect behavior - it just does nothing useful. The finding is accurate but represents incomplete implementation rather than a defect.

adjudication_records.issue_text: config/routes.rb:153 — Declaring unrestricted resources exposes four routes with no controller actions, so scope this resource to create, update, and destroy.

adjudication.rationale: The finding correctly identifies that line 153 in config/routes.rb adds `resources :embeddable_hosts` which by Rails convention creates 7 RESTful routes (index, show, new, create, edit, update, destroy). Looking at the controller in app/controllers/admin/embeddable_hosts_controller.rb, only create, update, and destroy actions are implemented. The index and show routes would return errors since those actions don't exist. While this isn't a security bug (the AdminConstraint protects all routes), it's a valid architectural concern - the resource declaration should be scoped to only the implemented actions using `only: [:create, :update, :destroy]` to avoid exposing non-functional routes.

adjudication_records.issue_text: app/assets/javascripts/admin/components/embeddable-host.js.es6:9 — Category state is duplicated across categoryId, host.category_id, and host.category and manually synchronized, so buffer one relationship field instead.

adjudication.rationale: The finding correctly identifies that the component maintains categoryId as separate state (line 9) that must be manually synchronized with host.category_id and host.category. In the save() action (lines 32-38), categoryId is used to set props.category_id, then after save, host.category is manually set by looking up the category. This is a valid architectural concern about state duplication that could lead to synchronization bugs, though the current implementation appears to work correctly.

adjudication_records.issue_text: app/assets/javascripts/discourse/models/store.js.es6:196 — The generic hydrator now deletes every *_ids field even when sideload lookups fail, so shared model hydration can silently discard unresolved relationship data.

adjudication.rationale: Looking at the diff in store.js.es6 lines 189-212, the new code handles `_ids` (plural) fields. When `m[2]` is truthy (meaning it matched `_ids`), it maps over the IDs and calls `_lookupSubType` for each. The result is assigned to `obj[self.pluralize(subType)]` and then `delete obj[k]` is called unconditionally. The issue is that if `_lookupSubType` returns undefined/null for any ID, those will be in the hydrated array, but more importantly, if the entire lookup mechanism fails or returns empty results, the original `_ids` field is still deleted. However, looking more carefully, the code does `hydrated || []` which provides a fallback empty array, and the delete happens regardless. This means if sideload data is missing, the original IDs are lost and replaced with an array that may contain undefined values. This is a real behavioral change that could cause data loss in the hydration process.

adjudication_records.issue_text: spec/controllers/admin/embeddable_hosts_controller_spec.rb:5 — The new controller spec asserts only its literal superclass declaration, leaving the new CRUD and default-category behavior without regression coverage.

adjudication.rationale: The finding correctly identifies that the new spec file at spec/controllers/admin/embeddable_hosts_controller_spec.rb only contains a single test asserting the controller inherits from AdminController. Looking at the diff, the actual controller (app/controllers/admin/embeddable_hosts_controller.rb) implements create, update, destroy actions with specific logic including default category assignment (line 24: 'host.category_id = SiteSetting.uncategorized_category_id if host.category_id.blank?'). This business logic has no test coverage in the new spec. This is a legitimate concern about missing test coverage for newly added nontrivial functionality.

adjudication_records.issue_text: app/models/embeddable_host.rb:17 — Every public embed request now performs an uncached `lower(host)` lookup that cannot use an index because the migration creates none, adding a database round-trip and table scan on this traffic-heavy path

adjudication.rationale: The finding is accurate. Looking at the diff, the migration in db/migrate/20150818190757_create_embeddable_hosts.rb creates the embeddable_hosts table but does not add any index on the host column. The EmbeddableHost.record_for_host method in app/models/embeddable_host.rb uses `where("lower(host) = ?", host)` which performs a case-insensitive lookup. Without an index on lower(host), this query will require a full table scan. This method is called on every embed request via EmbeddableHost.host_allowed? (used in embed_controller.rb and topic_retriever.rb), making it a performance issue on a potentially high-traffic path.

adjudication_records.issue_text: db/migrate/20150818190757_create_embeddable_hosts.rb:11 — The migration dereferences a missing embed-category query row before its fallback, so upgrades without a matching persisted embed_category crash.

adjudication.rationale: Looking at the migration code in db/migrate/20150818190757_create_embeddable_hosts.rb, lines 10-14 show: `category_id = execute("SELECT c.id FROM categories AS c INNER JOIN site_settings AS s ON s.value = c.name WHERE s.name = 'embed_category'")[0]['id'].to_i`. If the query returns no rows (no embed_category setting exists), then `[0]` returns nil, and calling `['id']` on nil will raise a NoMethodError. The fallback on lines 16-18 only triggers if `category_id == 0`, but the code crashes before reaching that check. This is a real bug that would cause migration failures for installations without an embed_category setting.

adjudication_records.issue_text: app/models/embeddable_host.rb:2 — Hosts have no uniqueness validation or index, so duplicate rows with different categories make record_for_host select an arbitrary category.

adjudication.rationale: The diff shows EmbeddableHost model at app/models/embeddable_host.rb with only a format validation on host (validates_format_of :host). There is no uniqueness validation. The record_for_host method uses .first to select a record, and the migration at db/migrate/20150818190757_create_embeddable_hosts.rb creates the table without a unique index on host. This means duplicate hosts with different categories can be inserted, and record_for_host will return an arbitrary one (whichever .first returns), leading to unpredictable category assignment for embedded topics.

adjudication_records.issue_text: app/assets/javascripts/admin/components/embeddable-host.js.es6:46 — The delete promise has no rejection handler, so failed deletions produce an unhandled error with no feedback or retry path.

adjudication.rationale: Looking at line 46 in app/assets/javascripts/admin/components/embeddable-host.js.es6, the delete action calls `this.get('host').destroyRecord().then(...)` but has no `.catch()` handler. In contrast, the save action on line 38 properly chains `.catch(popupAjaxError)` to handle errors. This is a real defect - if the delete API call fails, the promise rejection will be unhandled and the user will receive no feedback about the failure.

adjudication_records.issue_text: app/controllers/admin/embeddable_hosts_controller.rb:10 — Updating or deleting a host that disappeared concurrently dereferences nil and returns a 500 instead of a not-found response.

adjudication.rationale: Looking at the diff for app/controllers/admin/embeddable_hosts_controller.rb, the update method (lines 10-13) does `host = EmbeddableHost.where(id: params[:id]).first` and then calls `save_host(host)`. If no record is found, `host` will be nil. The `save_host` method then tries to call `host.host = params[:embeddable_host][:host]` which would raise a NoMethodError on nil, resulting in a 500 error instead of a proper 404 response. The same issue exists in the destroy method (lines 15-18) where `host.destroy` would be called on nil.

adjudication_records.issue_text: db/migrate/20150818190757_create_embeddable_hosts.rb:25 — Unescaped legacy host values are interpolated into migration SQL, allowing a crafted embeddable_hosts setting to execute arbitrary SQL during upgrade.

adjudication.rationale: The migration at line 25 uses string interpolation to insert host values directly into SQL: `execute "INSERT INTO embeddable_hosts (host, category_id, created_at, updated_at) VALUES ('#{h}', #{category_id}, CURRENT_TIMESTAMP, CURRENT_TIMESTAMP)"`. The host values come from a site setting that could contain malicious SQL. If an attacker had previously set embeddable_hosts to contain SQL injection payloads like `'); DROP TABLE users; --`, this would execute arbitrary SQL during the migration. This is a real SQL injection vulnerability in the migration code.

adjudication_records.issue_text: spec/controllers/admin/embeddable_hosts_controller_spec.rb:5 — The sole spec checks inheritance, leaving create/update/destroy persistence, category fallback, invalid input, missing IDs, and staff authorization unverified.

adjudication.rationale: The finding correctly identifies that the new spec file at spec/controllers/admin/embeddable_hosts_controller_spec.rb only contains a single test checking class inheritance ('is a subclass of AdminController'). Looking at the diff, the controller at app/controllers/admin/embeddable_hosts_controller.rb implements create, update, and destroy actions with specific logic including category_id fallback to uncategorized_category_id, but none of this functionality is tested. This is a legitimate concern about missing test coverage for newly added nontrivial logic.

adjudication_records.issue_text: app/models/topic_embed.rb:36 — No test imports content from different configured hosts and asserts that each resulting topic receives that host's category, leaving the feature's core behavior unverified.

adjudication.rationale: The finding correctly identifies that the new feature allowing different embeddable hosts to have different categories (seen in topic_embed.rb line 36: `category: eh.try(:category_id)`) lacks comprehensive test coverage. Looking at the test file spec/models/topic_embed_spec.rb, there's only one embeddable_host fabricated and the test only verifies that `post.topic.category` equals `embeddable_host.category`. There's no test that creates multiple embeddable hosts with different categories and verifies that importing from different hosts results in topics being assigned to the correct respective categories. This is a legitimate gap in test coverage for newly added nontrivial logic.

adjudication_records.issue_text: db/migrate/20150818190757_create_embeddable_hosts.rb:11 — No migration test covers a database without a persisted embed_category override, so the nil result dereference can abort upgrades on default configurations.

adjudication.rationale: The migration at line 11 executes a SQL query to find category_id by joining site_settings with categories. If no 'embed_category' setting exists (default configuration), the query returns an empty result set, and accessing [0]['id'] on nil/empty result would cause an error. The code then checks if category_id == 0 and falls back to uncategorized_category_id, but the initial dereference [0]['id'] on an empty result set would fail before reaching that check. This is a real bug in the migration that could affect default installations.

adjudication_records.issue_text: spec/controllers/embed_controller_spec.rb:69 — The multi-host test fabricates records through normalization callbacks, so it cannot catch legacy URL-form hosts that the migration inserts raw and that lookup can no longer match.

adjudication.rationale: The finding claims the test cannot catch legacy URL-form hosts that the migration inserts raw. However, looking at the diff: 1) The test in spec/controllers/embed_controller_spec.rb:69 uses Fabricate(:embeddable_host) which goes through the model's before_validation callback that strips 'http://' and 'https://' prefixes. 2) The EmbeddableHost model (app/models/embeddable_host.rb) has a before_validation that does `self.host.sub!(/^https?:\/\//, '')` to normalize hosts. 3) The migration (db/migrate/20150818190757_create_embeddable_hosts.rb) inserts hosts directly via SQL without going through the model callbacks, but this is a migration concern, not a test concern. 4) The test fabricates hosts like 'http://discourse.org' and 'https://example.com/1234' which will be normalized by the model callbacks. The finding conflates migration behavior with test behavior - the tests use Fabricate which does go through model callbacks and normalization.

adjudication_records.issue_text: app/assets/javascripts/admin/components/embeddable-host.js.es6:31 — No component or acceptance test exercises edit/save/cancel/delete or asserts the category_id request and resulting row state for the principal admin workflow.

adjudication.rationale: The diff introduces a new embeddable-host component with significant functionality (edit, save, cancel, delete actions, category selection, buffered content management). Looking at the test files added, spec/controllers/admin/embeddable_hosts_controller_spec.rb and spec/controllers/admin/embedding_controller_spec.rb only verify class inheritance. There are no JavaScript component tests or acceptance tests for the new admin UI workflow. The finding correctly identifies that the principal admin workflow for managing embeddable hosts lacks test coverage. This is a legitimate concern for newly added nontrivial logic.

adjudication_records.issue_text: app/assets/javascripts/discourse/models/store.js.es6:192 — The new global _ids hydration branch has no client unit coverage for resolved, missing, or empty IDs despite changing every REST-serialized model.

adjudication.rationale: The diff adds new logic in store.js.es6 (lines 192-209) to handle `_ids` plural hydration for embedded objects. The test file store-test.js.es6 is updated to test the happy path (colors array with valid IDs), but there's no test coverage for edge cases like: missing IDs in the lookup, empty ID arrays, or when _lookupSubType returns undefined for some IDs. The finding correctly identifies that this new branch lacks comprehensive test coverage for edge cases, though basic functionality is tested.
